section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Angular Sweep
section_1.content: Introduce the idea of a line rotating around a point (pivot). Explain that the 'Windmill' is a line pivoted at one point in a set of points, rotating until it hits another point.
section_1.example: A lighthouse beam (the line) rotating in the ocean, hitting different islands (the points) one by one.

section_2.title: Defining the Windmill Mechanics
section_2.content: Establish the rules: Given a set of points, pick one as a pivot. Rotate the line clockwise. When it hits a second point, that point becomes the new pivot, and the process repeats.
section_2.example: Visualizing a clock hand that snaps to a new center point every time it strikes a target marker.

section_3.title: Key Property: The Invariant of Order
section_3.content: Explain the core observation: The sequence of points encountered depends on the initial angle. Highlight that the number of 'swaps' can be predicted using geometry.
section_3.example: A chameleon on a rotating branch catching fireflies; the order of catches is determined by the starting orientation of the branch.

section_4.title: Visualization of the Rotation
section_4.content: Use a step-by-step animation sequence: (1) Select initial pivot, (2) Calculate angles to all other points, (3) Rotate line to smallest angle, (4) Update pivot. Focus on the geometry of the 'next hit'.
section_4.example: A spider web where the string (the line) rotates and attaches to the next nearest anchor point on the web.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-World Application
section_5.content: Summarize the computational complexity (O(N^2) or O(N log N) depending on optimization). Discuss applications in robotics pathfinding and sensor coverage.
section_5.example: A robot vacuum cleaner navigating a room filled with obstacles, using the windmill strategy to clear every corner.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give room for text
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
